subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Public Key Cryptography
description: A 60-second lesson on Public Key Cryptography.

hook.text: How do you share a secret with someone you've never met? Public key cryptography solved this puzzle.

buildup.text: Before the 1970s, both sender and receiver needed the same secret key. Sharing it safely was the weak point.

discovery.text: Diffie and Hellman proposed two keys: a public one for encrypting and a private one for decrypting.

twist.text: British intelligence actually invented the concept first — but kept it classified for decades.

climax.text: Public key cryptography made secure internet communication possible. Without it, there's no online banking.

punchline.text: Two keys solved a centuries-old problem.

quiz.question: What problem does public key cryptography solve?
options: Securely exchanging encrypted messages without pre-sharing a secret key
Eliminating the need for any encryption keys
